question_en:
I am verifying the material labels of elements in the diagram. Starting from the element cell at the far left of the third period, look up each independent element record in the illustrated database one by one and read `Element Classification`, `Physical Description`, and `Atomic Weight`. In each round, first judge: if `Physical Description` is exactly `Gas`, stop immediately; otherwise, move to the next cell according to the following rules: for `Metal` or `Non-metal`, move right along the same period; for `Semi-metal`, move up along the same group. When encountering a blank position, skip to the next actual existing element cell. Please answer the following questions:
1. Which elements were visited in order? List them as "Element Symbol—Element Name—Element Classification—Physical Description—Atomic Weight".
2. How many different element records were visited in total?
3. Which element did you finally stop at, and what field value triggered the stop?

Answer Format: Please answer in points numbered (1)–(3); for question 1, use a table to list the five element fields in order; for question 2, state the total number of records in text; for question 3, state the final element and the field value that triggered the stop in text.
answer:
(1)

| Visit Order | Element Symbol | Element Name | Element Classification | Physical Description | Atomic Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Na | Sodium | Metal | Solid | 22.989 769 28(2) |
| 2 | Mg | Magnesium | Metal | Solid | [24.304, 24.307] |
| 3 | Al | Aluminum | Metal | Solid | 26.981 5384(3) |
| 4 | Si | Silicon | Semi-metal | Solid | [28.084, 28.086] |
| 5 | C | Carbon | Non-metal | Solid | [12.0096, 12.0116] |
| 6 | N | Nitrogen | Non-metal | Gas | [14.006 43, 14.007 28] |

(2) A total of 6 different element records were visited.

(3) Finally stopped at N (Nitrogen); the field value that triggered the stop was Physical Description = Gas.
